questions.question: What is an element?
options: A substance made of only one type of atom
questions.answer: A substance made of only one type of atom
questions.explanation: An element contains only one type of atom, e.g. oxygen or iron.

questions.question: Which of these is a compound?
questions.explanation: Water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) contains hydrogen and oxygen chemically joined.

questions.question: How many atoms are in one molecule of $\text{CO}_2$?
questions.explanation: One carbon atom and two oxygen atoms: 3 atoms.

questions.question: Elements in the same group of the periodic table ...
options: were discovered at the same time
questions.explanation: Elements in a group react in similar ways, e.g. the alkali metals.

questions.question: Where are the metals found on the periodic table?
options: On the left and in the middle
questions.answer: On the left and in the middle
questions.explanation: Metals are on the left and centre; non-metals are on the right.

questions.question: Magnesium burns in oxygen. What is the product?
questions.explanation: Magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide.

questions.question: In a sealed flask, 10 g of reactants react. What is the mass of the products?
questions.explanation: Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, so mass is conserved.

questions.question: Where is most water absorbed back into the body?
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water from undigested food.

questions.question: What do enzymes do in digestion?
options: Break large molecules into small ones the body can absorb
questions.answer: Break large molecules into small ones the body can absorb
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts that break down large food molecules.

questions.question: What is the word equation for aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen to release energy from glucose.

questions.question: What is produced by anaerobic respiration in human muscles?
questions.explanation: Without enough oxygen, muscles make lactic acid.

questions.question: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (using light).

questions.question: Where does gas exchange happen in the lungs?
questions.explanation: Oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse across the thin walls of the alveoli.

questions.question: What is the unit of resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

questions.question: A bulb has a current of 0.5 A and a potential difference of 6 V. What is its resistance?
questions.explanation: $R = V \div I = 6 \div 0.5 = 12$ Ω.

questions.question: What happens when two north poles are brought together?
questions.explanation: Like poles repel; opposite poles attract.

questions.question: Why is a sharp knife better at cutting than a blunt one?
options: The force acts on a smaller area, giving higher pressure
questions.answer: The force acts on a smaller area, giving higher pressure
questions.explanation: Pressure = force ÷ area; a thin edge means a small area and high pressure.

questions.question: A train travels 180 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
How is heat mainly transferred through a metal spoon?
questions.explanation: In solids, vibrating particles pass energy along: conduction.

questions.question: Which of these makes a test fair?
questions.explanation: Only change the independent variable; keep everything else the same.
